taxpayer.notes: IRA held with Capital Guardian, LLC / Pershing, LLC (custodian), account ending 0946.

adjustments: IRA distribution of $524,980 included in gross income (rollover not within 60 days)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Whether the IRA distribution was timely rolled over
conceded: Petitioner (deemed, Rule 34(b)(4)): $337 HSA distribution and §223(f)(4)(A) additional tax

findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioner received a $524,981.89 distribution from the IRA with an account number ending in 0946.

findings_of_fact.fact: Intended to roll over within 60 days; used funds to buy home pending sale of former home
findings_of_fact.snippet: She intended to roll over the distribution back into her IRA within 60 days of receipt.

findings_of_fact.fact: On Aug 21, 2014 received $524,981 cashier's check payable to Pershing FBO petitioner and overnighted it to Capital Guardian
findings_of_fact.snippet: On Thursday, August 21, 2014, petitioner overnighted the check to Capital Guardian.

findings_of_fact.fact: Check arrived at Capital Guardian Friday, August 22, 2014, 58 days after distribution
findings_of_fact.snippet: on Friday, August 22, which was 58 days after petitioner received the IRA distribution.

findings_of_fact.fact: Deposited into IRA on August 26, 2014, 62 days after distribution
findings_of_fact.snippet: On August 26, 2014, 62 days after petitioner received the IRA distribution, the check was deposited at Pershing

findings_of_fact.fact: Capital Guardian assured petitioner she could roll over by overnighting check to it; Capital Guardian was an appropriate institution; late recording was a bookkeeping error
findings_of_fact.snippet: we find that the late recording is due to a bookkeeping error.

findings_of_fact.fact: Notice dated February 27, 2017 included $524,980 in income
findings_of_fact.snippet: the Commissioner determined that petitioner was required to include $524,980 of the IRA distribution in her 2014 gross income.

findings_of_fact.fact: Funds deposited into IRA within one year
findings_of_fact.snippet: In this case the funds were deposited into petitioner's IRA within one year.

issues.question: Did petitioner roll over the June 25, 2014 IRA distribution within 60 days so that it is excluded from 2014 gross income?
issues.holding: Yes: check received by Capital Guardian on day 58 and late book entry (day 62) was a bookkeeping error, so rollover timely; alternatively, petitioner qualifies for automatic hardship waiver (deposited within 1 year; would have been valid rollover had institution deposited as instructed)
issues.computable_reason: Given the finding that delivery to Capital Guardian counts as deposit (bookkeeping error), 58 <= 60 days is mechanical; alternative automatic waiver conditions are also mechanical.

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: IRA distribution qualifies as rollover (not taxable); HSA items conceded by petitioner; no 6662(a) penalty (conceded).

notes: Key judgment: Capital Guardian (not custodian Pershing) was an appropriate institution to receive the check — factual finding relying partly on credited testimony. Notice included $524,980, not the full $524,981.89 (unexplained).
